newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore on track for 7-8 percent growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Singapore on track for 7-8 percent growth in 1996.

text.p: Singapore is on track to achieve projected economic growth of 7-8 percent in 1996, Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong said on Tuesday.
Yeo also told reporters he expected an electronics industry rebound in the first half of 1997.
"The trade figures are going to be fairly volatile for the next few months," Yeo said after a plant opening ceremony.
"From the present trend, I think we are still pretty much on track for the 7 to 8 percent (economic growth this year)."

Asked when the current downturn in the electronics industry would end, Yeo replied that "based on discussions with industry leaders, we expect to see some recovery taking place early next year -- in the first six months."
He said that "should translate into higher trade growth for us as well, so we're watching the first half of next year with great interest".
Yeo said the Singapore government had anticipated a downturn in the electronics industry and was not disappointed in recent data.

"In a way, the slowdown in the electronics industry was pretty well forecast by the industry itself. It didn't really come as a surprise and, as we all know from the bigger cycles, the electronic downturns can be very rapid just as the upturns can be very rapid."
Asked if there were more bad trade figures in store for Singapore, Yeo said: "I wish I knew."

"Talking to the companies, I think many of them are quite optimistic that we are near the trough, so even if there is a further downturn it shouldn't be too dramatic. But I think quite a few are optimistic that we have leveled off," Yeo said.
On Friday, Singapore reported its exports fell 4.4 percent in August, more sharply than expected by many economists.

Singapore's Trade Development Board blamed the fall on the slowdown in global demand for electronics and related products as well as an oversupply of semiconductors. Electronics account for almost half Singapore's total industrial output and around 60 percent of non-oil exports. -- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
